narrative_arc: 22-year-old adventurer Poppy sails for Ironbeard's legendary treasure and finds it, but a rival pirate captain and crew who tailed her steal it and mock her → fleeing belowdecks she finds glowing 'spinach' capsules, drinks one, and temporarily grows into a hyper-muscular powerhouse → she thrashes the captain's crew and reclaims the treasure, then the power fades and she shrinks back to normal and sails off → the defeated captain wakes, finds the spinach trail, and feeds it to herself and her whole crew → they permanently bulk up into a hyper-muscular gang and rally for revenge (TO BE CONTINUED into issue 2).

panels.notes: Bird's-eye establishing shot: a distant sailboat crosses open water toward a tropical island; caption box sets the 22-year-old-Poppy/first-adventure premise.
Full-body helm shot; wind-blown hair and an off-shoulder collar establish a confident-adventurer pose, with a large foreground ship's wheel adding depth.
Treasure-map inset with a red circle marking the target island; dialogue balloon establishes the legendary-strength macguffin.
Close flex on the gripping fist and raised forearm/bicep while tearing the map fragment; teeth-gritted expression sells effort, with strain lines tracing the arm.
Wide traveling shot: the sailboat cuts spray toward the island past a distant carved rock/statue marker, with birds in the sky; the 'LAND HO!' balloon signals the arrival beat.

pages.page_notes: distance_spread=4; flat_panel_count=1; Setup page establishing 22-year-old Poppy's voyage toward Ironbeard's treasure/legendary-strength macguffin; only muscle-forward beat is the panel 4 bicep flex on 'GRIT'; the rest is scene-setting and travel wide shots with no growth depicted yet.

panels.notes: Full-width establishing shot of a jungle-covered island with a hidden cave mouth; speaker is off-panel (balloon points down from below frame), no character actually in shot.
Foreground figure holding a raised torch against a background cave chamber stacked with treasure chests; torch and raised arm form the panel's main diagonal.
Full-body straining carry pose, eyes shut and mouth open in effort, sweat beads flung outward, played for comedic/ironic weakness ahead of a strength payoff later in the issue.

Grayscale reveal panel: a heavily-built silhouetted figure fills most of the frame, backlit by bright cave light, while a second figure's head/hair is visible cut off in the near foreground corner for scale. No face detail on either figure is renderable — this is a pure silhouette/rim-light reveal.

pages.page_notes: distance_spread=3; flat_panel_count=1; Page opens on a static, figure-less establishing shot of a hidden cave mouth, cuts to Poppy discovering a treasure chamber by torchlight, drops into a strained solo full-body carry as she hauls one chest out, and ends on a desaturated silhouette reveal of an unknown, heavily-built figure confronting her mid-panel — a scene-setting page building to a cliffhanger threat rather than delivering an active-growth beat.

panels.notes: Captain fills the frame chest-up while two crew stand small and soft-focused behind her, selling her size before any growth is shown.

Static reaction close-up; one eye rendered blank white for shock. A small yellow spark/crown-shaped symbol floats above her head -- unclear whether it's a generic shock icon or a story-relevant crown, flagged for review.
No figure; nested inset shows the treasure chest falling, with vertical motion-streak lines and jagged impact bursts around it, wedged in the gutter between the two flanking character panels.
Waist-up power stance, one hand hooked on her hip belt, both bulging arms fully in frame while she needles Poppy about being tailed for months.

Seen from behind/side, forearm and fist thrust into extreme foreground with a double 'TREMBLE' SFX (two colors) flanking the bent, crossed arms; her face is not clearly readable from this angle, so the emotion word is inferred from body language only.
Same waist-up power framing as the earlier captain panel; head tips back mid-laugh, mocking Poppy's declaration. This inset floats on the unframed fist backdrop rather than sitting in its own gutter.

pages.page_notes: distance_spread=4; flat_panel_count=1; Two-beat confrontation page -- the captain's crew reveals they've tailed Poppy for months and are taking the treasure, Poppy protests then flares into a trembling fist-clenched 'it's all mine' declaration, and the captain answers with a mocking laugh. Power imbalance is sold mainly through scale-contrast and tight power-stance crops on the captain; no panel on this page is an active-growth money shot, staging stays reaction/dialogue-driven throughout.

pages.page_notes: distance_spread=1; flat_panel_count=0; Issue-2 cover, excluded from issue-1's growth-page ratio. strengths: The book runs TWO complete transformation arcs off one Popeye-pastiche mechanic (spinach = strength) instead of one-and-done: Poppy's temporary growth (p5-8) pays off in a fight then visibly fades (p10), and the captain's crew's permanent growth (p12-17) pays off in a cliffhanger rally -- doubling the growth-page count without repeating the same beat.

The 'flex ladder' -- the exact same double-biceps pose redrawn 3x at increasing panel scale -- is a dead-simple, highly legible escalation device used twice (p8 panels 2-4; p14 panels 2-4). Directly reusable as a 3-shot CGI sequence.

p13's progressive body-part ECU column (chest→chest→abs→glutes across 4 sequential panels, unified by one continuous lightning-bolt motif and stacked SWELL/BULGE/RIIIP sfx) is a clean, reusable multi-panel-progressive template.

The dynamic camera bias is not reserved for money shots -- even p1 panel 4, a plain map-tearing beat with zero growth content, gets a low-angle chest-height bicep flex. Only 6 of 79 panels (7.6%) are flat-level across the whole book.

SFX chains (BULGE/RIIIP/SWELL/BOING, heaviest p13-14 and p16-17) carry growth sensation cheaply even when a panel goes faceless or backgroundless -- the zoom-escalation device works because the sfx does real narrative work, not just noise.

Scale-contrast onlookers sell the size payoff economically: tiny reacting pirates below Poppy's silhouette (p9 panels 2-3) and a normal-scale captain flanked by hyper-muscular crew in the closing splash (p17 panel 3) sell scale without needing a ruler or prop.
weaknesses: Faceless growth ECUs recur in both arcs -- p7 panels 2 & 4, p8 panel 1, p13 panels 3-4, p14 panel 1 -- the same 'money-shot goes faceless' defect flagged in the ultragal comparison comic. A cut-in reaction face during these body-part ECUs would close the gap cheaply (the book already does this well elsewhere, e.g. p13 panel 2, p14 panels 3-4).

Pages 9-11 sag the pacing: after Poppy's growth peaks on p8, the book spends a fight (p9), a fade-out (p10), and a slow re-discovery walk (p11) before Act 2's growth restarts on p12 -- three pages of connective tissue right after the first payoff cool the momentum.

Panel-boundary legibility gets shaky on the busiest layout pages -- p3's borderless energy backdrop with floating insets, p11's giant foreground object spanning two tiers, and p12's two growth beats merged into one wide panel were all flagged as genuine reading-order judgment calls by the analysts; worth a human pass to confirm intended order.

The 'muscle literally breaks the panel border' trick (p8 panel 4, p14 panel 4) is a 2D-only flourish -- it reads as scale in ink but has no single-camera equivalent; a CGI version needs a substitute (extreme frame-crop / foreground-fills-lens) rather than a literal border break.

Distance monotony inside both growth bursts: pages 6, 7, 8, 13 and 14 each hold to only 2 distinct shot_distances, trading shot-size variety for zoom intensity -- effective as a choice, but it means camera dynamism on those pages is carried entirely by staging/angle, not by distance variety.
